# User-Defined Template Output Reference

Complete reference for rendering a read command's result through your own Go `text/template` — a widening of the `-o`/`--output` flag's value set beyond the four built-in formats.

## Overview

This capability **adds no command and no flag**. It widens what a *value* of the existing `-o`/`--output` flag may mean: in addition to the four built-in format tokens, the flag value may be a **path to a template file** or the literal **`stdin`** (read a template from a pipe). The flag itself — its short alias `-o`, its scope, and its precedence — is unchanged.

A user template is shaped to one resource type, so the widened vocabulary is **flag-only**: `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` and the `.glassfrogrc output` key still accept only the four tokens.

Codebase enrichment skipped — not attempted. This reference is based on the interface contract and the shipped `-o` usage string.

## Widened `-o` / `--output` value set

The value is interpreted (flag rung only) as:

| Flag value | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| `full` \| `compact` \| `json` \| `yaml` (case-insensitive) | a built-in format (unchanged) |
| `stdin` | read a user template from piped standard input |
| any other non-empty value | a path to a user template file (relative paths resolved against the current working directory) |

- **Reserved names win.** The four format tokens **and** `stdin` are reserved. A file literally named `full`, `json`, or `stdin` in the working directory is **not** selected by bare name — reference it with a path, e.g. `-o ./stdin`.
- **Flag-only.** The widened vocabulary applies only to the `-o`/`--output` **flag value**. `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` and `.glassfrogrc output` keep the four-token contract — any other value there is a usage error naming that source, **not** treated as a template path.
- **Shipped usage string**: `Output format — full | compact | json | yaml, a template file path, or "stdin" to read a template from a pipe (overrides GLASSFROG_OUTPUT, the .glassfrogrc output, and the built-in default)`.

## Affected commands

Every result-producing read that resolves `-o` — `me` / `me roles` / `me actions` / `me projects`, `roles` / `role` / `tree` / `subroles`, `domains` / `domain`, `policies` / `policy`, `projects` / `project`, and every future `--output`-capable read. The command synopsis is unchanged (the `-o <value>` slot already exists). Commands that produce no result data (`auth login`, `version`) are unaffected by `-o`.

## What a user template puts on stdout

| Selection | stdout |
|---|---|
| `-o ./tmpl` (file) | whatever the template emits when executed against the command's result value |
| `-o stdin` (pipe) | same — the template read from the pipe, executed against the result value |

There is no fixed stdout shape — the template *is* the shape. The one floor is **anti-fabrication**: a template can only project data the result carried; it cannot make the CLI emit a value the API did not return. Templates are parsed with `missingkey=error`, so an unguarded reference to an absent field fails loudly rather than rendering silent fake data.

Templates are parsed into a clone of the built-in template set, so a user template may invoke a built-in by name, e.g. `{{template "roles.full.tmpl" .}}`.

### Examples

```
# template file
glassfrog me roles -o ./role-ids.tmpl

# piped template
printf '{{range .Roles}}{{.ID}}\n{{end}}' | glassfrog me roles -o stdin

# reserved name wins over a same-named file
glassfrog me -o full        # the built-in full projection — a file named "full" is NOT read
```

## Resolution and timing

- **Precedence (unchanged)**: `-o`/`--output` flag → `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` → `.glassfrogrc output` → built-in default `full`. The flag short-circuits the lower rungs. A template source can arise **only** at the flag rung.
- **Accepted anywhere on the path**: `glassfrog -o ./t.tmpl me roles` and `glassfrog me roles -o ./t.tmpl` resolve identically.
- **Parsed before any request**: when the flag selects a template source, the CLI reads the source (file or piped stdin) and **parses** it before assembling the connection or sending — so a missing file, malformed template, or empty/un-piped stdin fails fast with no API request. The template is **executed** only after a successful response.

## Exit codes and errors

All template-source failures map to a **usage error (exit `2`)** — the same class as a malformed `--output` token. No new exit code is introduced. Messages are token-free and name the source and a corrective next step.

| Condition | stdout | Exit | Request made? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Template (file or stdin) renders successfully | the template's output | 0 | Yes |
| `-o ./nope.tmpl` — file missing / unreadable | nothing | 2 | No |
| `-o ./broken.tmpl` / piped template — fails to **parse** | nothing | 2 | No |
| `-o stdin` — no pipe (interactive TTY) or empty pipe | nothing | 2 | No |
| Template parses but fails at **execution** (unguarded reference to an absent field) | nothing | 2 | **Yes** (post-response) |
| `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` / `.glassfrogrc output` holds a non-token value (flag absent) | nothing | 2 | No |
| Read itself fails (transport/API/auth/decode) | per the failing read | existing (1/3/4/5/6) | — |

The post-response execution case is the one path that spends a request before exiting `2` — unavoidable because `text/template` field existence is only knowable at execution time. On any parse or execution failure, nothing partial reaches stdout (buffer-then-write).
